articles.title: Ancient Gallo-Roman wall found beneath Paris's Île de la Cité could confirm site of Lutetia, city's first settlement, ministry says
articles.summary: An ancient wall unearthed beneath the courtyards of Paris's Hôtel-Dieu hospital has been described as a \"major breakthrough\" by France's culture ministry,
articles.body: An ancient wall unearthed beneath the courtyards of Paris's Hôtel-Dieu hospital has been described as a "major breakthrough" by France's culture ministry, with the archaeological find possibly confirming the location of the city's original settlement. The roughly 65-foot wall, dating from the Gallo-Roman period, was discovered this summer on the Île de la Cité, a stone's throw from Notre Dame Cathedral in the heart of the city.What the newly discovered wall could reveal about the lost Gallic settlement of LutetiaThe stone-and-wood find is thought to be a fragment of the ramparts of Lutetia, the ancient name for Paris, built by the Gallic Parisii tribe, who lived along the river Seine during the Iron Age. The Guardian reported that Lutetia was first mentioned in book seven of Julius Caesar's "Gallic Wars," where it was described only vaguely as being on an island in the Seine, a detail that has fueled decades of debate over the settlement's exact location.Why archaeologists have long debated whether Lutetia stood on the island or in NanterreThe Île de la Cité has traditionally been regarded as the centre of Lutetia, but a rival theory, backed by archaeological research, contends that it was instead in Nanterre, a suburb to the west. Regional archaeology curator Stéphane Deschamps said the new find helps settle that long-running question, noting that, lacking tangible evidence on the island itself, some researchers had even proposed Nanterre as the true site, a gap this wall and its surrounding context may finally close.How excavators uncovered the fire-scarred wall beneath a working Paris hospitalThe wall emerged from excavations that began in February 2026 ahead of a restructuring of the Hôtel-Dieu hospital, with the dig led by David Couturier of the City of Paris archaeology department, supported by France's National Institute for Preventive Archaeological Research (Inrap). Heritage curator Dorothée Chaoui-Derieux said the wall's large blocks and interlocking beam system immediately pointed to Gallic construction traditions rather than a later Roman build.Archaeologists also found a roughly six-foot-thick platform of sand and gravel behind the wall that may have reinforced it, along with burned seeds and a Gallic spearhead nearby. The wall bears traces of fire, which may correspond to Caesar's account that the Gauls set fire to their own town before the Battle of Lutetia against the Romans. Carbon dating of the charred evidence places it between roughly 10 and 200 BC, a timeframe that encompasses the Battle of Lutetia in 52 BC. Fire had blackened the wall's outer face and destroyed a wooden structure standing just in front of it.What French officials are saying about the significance of the discovery"We may be looking at one of the most important remains ever discovered for understanding Gallic Lutetia," Culture Minister Catherine Pégard said in a statement from her ministry. She added that scientific caution still requires verifying the wall's function and chronology, but that the convergence of evidence is particularly remarkable at this stage. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire visited the excavation site as the findings were announced this week.How this fits into a string of recent archaeological finds tied to Notre Dame CathedralNotre Dame itself has yielded numerous archaeological finds in recent years. In June, officials announced the discovery of multiple artefacts, including a fourth-century coin and mysterious inscriptions, while in 2022, archaeologists uncovered several tombs and a sarcophagus likely dating from the 14th century. Researchers say further excavation at the Hôtel-Dieu site will focus on determining what the wall was built for, when it was constructed and abandoned, and what remains buried beneath the reinforcing platform behind it.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘My mom dies alone’: Belgian trekker recounts how a legal battle in India kept him away from his dying mother
articles.summary: In June 2024, Belgian trekker and Chennai-based activist Peter Van Geit lost his 93-year-old mother, Irena Van Goethem.
articles.body: In June 2024, Belgian trekker and Chennai-based activist Peter Van Geit lost his 93-year-old mother, Irena Van Goethem. She died in Belgium, where Van Geit had wanted to be with her during her final years.Instead, he says, he was in India, after years of legal proceedings stemming from a 2018 trekking expedition that ended in a devastating forest fire in Tamil Nadu.“Mom, 93 years, dies alone. Her only son stuck in India,” Van Geit wrote in an Instagram carousel recently, recounting the events that, according to him, kept him away from his mother for years.His post is a chronological account of what he describes as a six-year legal and personal ordeal- beginning with the Kurangani forest fire, followed by an arrest warrant, five weeks on the run, a confiscated passport and repeated court appearances, before the Supreme Court eventually quashed the criminal proceedings against him.From trekking club to tragedyVan Geit founded the Chennai Trekking Club (CTC) in 2008. He describes it as a non-profit volunteer group that was involved in trekking and social-service activities.In March 2018, a group went trekking in the Kurangani hills of Tamil Nadu. A forest fire broke out in the area, trapping trekkers.The tragedy claimed multiple lives.Van Geit’s recent Instagram post says 23 people died. (However, figures have varied in different accounts of the incident. The Supreme Court's 2024 judgment records 13 deaths).Van Geit maintains that the trek had been organised with the required permission. In his Instagram account, he says that after the tragedy, questions turned towards responsibility for the deaths. He also refers to a report on the Kurangani forest fire which, according to him, placed responsibility on Tamil Nadu forest officials. Then, he says, his own legal troubles began.‘Witch hunt begins’Van Geit recalls that he was running a 190-km route from Chennai to Auroville when he learnt that an arrest warrant had been issued against him. The words he uses in his post are stark: “Witch hunt begins.” He says his lawyer warned him: “Peter run! They’ll arrest you.” Van Geit then describes driving around 1,000 km to the Belgian Embassy, apparently seeking help. According to his account, the response was not what he had hoped for. He writes simply: “Embassy: get lost.”What followed, he says, was five weeks of uncertainty.“Man hunt begins,” he writes, listing what he describes as political pressure, his account being frozen, media blaming him and police chasing him. For five weeks, he says, he remained on the run. Eventually, the High Court granted him bail. But the case did not end there.A passport he could not useVan Geit says his passport was confiscated, preventing him from travelling to Belgium. That became particularly significant as his mother grew older. He describes the next six years as a period of “countless court hearings”, along with a financial loss of around ₹50 lakh. Meanwhile, his mother was ageing in Belgium.In 2023, Van Geit says, a doctor gave him news that changed the urgency of his fight. “Mom is dying. 4th stage cancer,” he wrote. His mother was then around 92.Van Geit publicly appealed for permission to travel to Belgium and see her. The appeal gathered support. In his Instagram post, he says 30,000 people signed a petition asking that he be allowed to visit his mother.The case also attracted attention in Belgium. In June 2023, The News Minute reported on Van Geit’s appeal, quoting him as saying that his mother lived alone and was unaware of the full extent of his legal troubles. “I am the only son,” he said at the time.Permission finally comesThe issue eventually reached the High Court, which granted Van Geit permission to travel to Belgium. For him, it meant something much more personal than simply leaving India.He had not seen his mother for years. Van Geit describes what followed in his Instagram carousel as a “happy reunion after 5 years.” It was a reunion he had spent years trying to make happen. But even then, the legal case in India was not over.Supreme Court ends the caseIn January 2024, the Supreme Court dealt with Van Geit’s case. The court examined the allegations and the material in the case and ultimately quashed the FIR and criminal proceedings against him. The judgment held that the trekkers had been caught in a forest fire, which was a natural event, and found that negligence could not be attributed to Van Geit in connection with the deaths.The court also noted that there was no material showing that Van Geit had caused the deaths or had played a role in the fire. Van Geit summarises the outcome in his own words: “Case dismissed. Force majeure. Peter is innocent.” Legally, the important point is that the Supreme Court quashed the proceedings against him; the judgment did not use the phrase “Peter is innocent” as a formal declaration. It found that the criminal proceedings could not be sustained against him.After years of legal uncertainty, the case was finally over.But his mother did not have much time leftThere was, however, another clock that had been running throughout those years. His mother’s. Van Geit says that even after the court case was dismissed, legal and immigration-related delays continued.Then came June 2024. His mother died in Belgium at the age of 93. The final part of Van Geit’s Instagram post is considerably quieter than the account of the years that preceded it. There is no description of another court hearing or another legal battle.Just her name on a gravestone: “Irena Van Goethem (1931–2024). And his words: “Jun 2024 - Mom dies alone.”For Van Geit, the Kurangani fire had begun as a tragedy involving a trekking group. What followed, according to his account, became a six-year struggle through arrests, bail, court hearings and travel restrictions.By the time the legal battle finally ended, he had already spent years separated from his mother. He did get to see her once more after the High Court granted him permission to travel - a reunion he describes as happy.But in June 2024, when she died, her only son was not beside her. That is the part of the story Van Geit appears to remember most starkly. Not the arrest warrant. Not the five weeks on the run. Not even the eventual Supreme Court victory. But the line with which he ends his account: “Mom dies alone.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump sought to play down Taiwan as a major point of friction with China after his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, saying
articles.body: US President Donald Trump sought to play down Taiwan as a major point of friction with China after his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, saying the two leaders did not discuss the issue in detail despite it being one of the most sensitive flashpoints in US-China ties.“We didn't talk about Taiwan too much with Xi. Right now, it's, you know, fine. It's just moving along. Xi understands very much how I feel,” Trump told reporters.Trump and Xi met at the White House last week as the two countries sought to stabilise ties after months of tensions over trade, technology and other geopolitical issues. The summit produced an extension of the US-China trade truce, while differences over Taiwan, artificial intelligence and Iran remained unresolved.Trump’s remarks came even as Taiwan continues to wait for Washington’s approval of a proposed $14 billion arms package, which has been held up for months. The package was reportedly put on hold after Trump’s meeting with Xi in Beijing earlier this year, and the US president has so far not indicated whether it will move forward following the latest summit.Ahead of the Washington talks, Beijing had made clear that Taiwan remained a “red line” and had pressed the United States to halt arms sales to the self-governed island, which China claims as its own territory. Xi was expected to raise the issue directly with Trump as part of broader discussions on trade, technology and regional security.Taipei, meanwhile, sought to reassure domestic audiences that US support remained intact. Taiwan deputy foreign minister Chen Ming-chi said Washington “very much” understands the island’s defence requirements and the military pressure it faces from China, adding that both sides remain in close communication.US law requires Washington to provide Taiwan with defensive capabilities, but the delay in the latest arms package has become a closely watched test of how Trump balances efforts to stabilise ties with Beijing against longstanding American support for Taipei.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Don't go back like this': Pakistan minister's throat-cut gesture to Afghan journalist backfires - video
articles.summary: Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif has faced criticism on social media over a threat-like gesture he made towards an Afghan woman journalist who
articles.body: Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif has faced criticism on social media over a threat-like gesture he made towards an Afghan woman journalist who questioned him about Pakistan's ties with the Taliban and its response to the treatment of Afghan women.The incident took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.The video clearly shows that journalist asked Asif what message Pakistan had for the Taliban over their policies toward Afghan women and why Islamabad had not challenged those policies when the Taliban were considered friends."What's your message to the Taliban now? To change their policy towards Afghan women? Why at the beginning, Pakistan didn't teach them that," the journalist asked, according to a video of the exchange shared on social media.Asif interrupted her without answering the question and pointed towards her attire."Don't go back like this over there. They will... otherwise they will..," he said, while making a hand gesture across his neck.The gesture drew strong condemnation online, with several social media users saying it appeared to imply that the journalist could be killed if she returned to Afghanistan. Users also criticised Asif and the men accompanying him for laughing after his remarks.A user on X wrote: "This is an utterly disgraceful way for a senior government minister to respond to a woman asking a serious question.""A woman asking about the suffering of Afghan women deserved an answer not intimidation, mockery, and laughter," he added.The journalist's question centred on the Taliban's policies towards Afghan women and Pakistan's position on them. Social media users said the response and the gesture were inappropriate and appeared to carry a threat of violence.The incident comes amid fresh tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with Islamabad carrying out aerial and drone strikes inside Afghanistan early Thursday.The Taliban also confirmed to news agency Reuters that 28 "fighters" were killed after crossing from Pakistan into eastern Afghanistan. The ruling-authority in Kabul also added that most of them were former Afghan security personnel.Pakistan called the strikes as "precision attacks" on 10 locations. Federal information minister Atauallah Tarar said the operation was carried out in response to drones launched from Afghanistan a day earlier.According to Dawn, Tarar said in a post on X that the strikes targeted locations allegedly used for launching and storing drones. He described the operation as "deliberate, precise, calibrated and proportionate and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan".Afghanistan has warned Pakistan of "dire consequences" over the strikes, describing them as blatant aggression."In this criminal aggression, four of our fellow Afghan compatriots have been martyred. The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan strongly condemns these blind and cowardly attacks in the harshest terms, considering them a flagrant violation of all principles, a blatant aggression, and a crime," Afghan government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said.Cross-border hostilities between the two neighbours have continued in recent weeks, with Pakistan carrying out military action, including aerial strikes, inside Afghanistan.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kapil Sibal alleges ‘unilateral’ EC decisions, seeks action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal on Sunday escalated the political row over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), accusing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal on Sunday escalated the political row over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), accusing chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of taking "unilateral decisions" and demanding his removal from office.Sibal also urged the Supreme Court to examine the Election Commission's records, dissent notes and orders issued during the period under question, and consider nullifying elections conducted during the 10-month period he referred to.The former Union minister's remarks came amid a controversy over internal objections raised by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi regarding decisions related to electoral rolls, the EC's IT systems and the SIR exercise.Sibal alleges unilateral decision-makingAccording to Sibal, the Election Commission's own statement issued on Saturday acknowledged that decisions had not been taken unanimously over the past several months. He alleged that Kumar had taken decisions "unilaterally" rather than through the full three-member Commission.Sibal claimed that Commission meetings were conducted without agendas being circulated or minutes being recorded, preventing the other commissioners from reviewing or commenting on decisions.He said the alleged practices covered 10 months, including elections held in Bihar in June 2025 and West Bengal in April.The allegations follow a report by The Indian Express, which said Sandhu and Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders that they said were issued without their knowledge.Sibal also alleged that decisions concerning additions and deletions of voters were centralised in Delhi through ECI NET under Seema Khanna, who managed its operations, instead of being handled by statutory Electoral Registration Officers.He demanded that an FIR be registered against Khanna and that she be arrested, arguing that unlike the CEC, she does not have statutory immunity from criminal prosecution.Sibal also alleged that changes were made to Form 6, used for new voter registration, requiring details of parents or grandparents without the central government issuing the required notification.EC responds to concerns over SIR and electoral rollsThe Election Commission on Saturday announced several decisions addressing issues that Sandhu and Joshi had raised in their internal communications.On Form 6, the EC said the additional declaration requiring new voters to provide details of their own or their parents' or grandparents' entries in the electoral roll from the previous SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.It said the additional requirement was specific to the SIR exercise and that regular statutory forms would continue to be used outside an SIR.On access to electoral-roll databases, the EC said field officers have role-based access to ECINET according to their statutory powers. It also announced a review by a committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner and including an independent IIT or IIIT expert to "double-check" the system's compliance with election laws and rules.The Commission further said agendas for all meetings would be circulated in advance and minutes issued, while directions issued by commissioners to EC officers would be complied with.On the IT division, the EC said disputed changes in the distribution of work were never implemented after Sandhu and Joshi intervened, and that oversight of the division by the deputy election commissioner was never withdrawn.Sibal, however, claimed that the alleged irregularities meant elections conducted from Bihar through West Bengal during the period were "illegal". He called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter and consider whether recent elections should be annulled.The opposition has also demanded Kumar's removal and an independent review of decisions and electoral-roll changes made during his tenure.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Marriage does not advance a child’s age': Delhi HC rejects Muslim personal law defence in POCSO case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to quash a POCSO case against a man who married a 16-year-old girl, holding that a marriage claimed to be
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to quash a POCSO case against a man who married a 16-year-old girl, holding that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot shield an adult from prosecution for sexual intercourse with a wife below 18.Justice Sanjeev Narula said the statutory age of 18 under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) cannot be replaced by the concept of puberty under personal law. “Put simply, marriage does not advance a child’s age. A person who is sixteen before the ceremony remains sixteen afterwards," he said, as quoted by ANI.The court was dealing with a petition filed by Bilal and another seeking quashing of FIR No. 189/2026 registered at Darya Ganj Police Station under Section 64(1) of the BNS and Section 6 of the POCSO Act. The petitioners had also sought disciplinary action against police officials and compensation for alleged false implication and harassment.According to the judgment, the girl was born on September 19, 2008, and married Bilal on December 20, 2024, when she was 16 years and three months old. Bilal was born on January 1, 1997 and was nearly 28 at the time. The couple subsequently lived together and the girl became pregnant. By May 2026, she was around eight months pregnant. Her age came to the notice of authorities when she visited a government hospital during her pregnancy.The foetus later died in utero and the girl delivered a stillborn child on June 6, 2026. The judgment records that an order was subsequently obtained from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for exhumation of the child for DNA profiling and collection of evidence.The FIR was not based on an allegation made by the girl herself. She maintained that the marriage had taken place with the consent of both families, that she had married of her own free will and that physical relations began after the marriage. She also supported Bilal during his bail proceedings and expressed a desire to have him by her side during her pregnancy.The petitioners argued that under Muslim personal law, a Muslim of sound mind who has attained puberty is competent to marry and that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, puberty is presumed after the age of 15. They contended that since the girl had attained puberty before the nikah, the marriage was valid and the subsequent sexual relationship could not attract criminal liability.The High Court rejected the argument, observing, “Personal law may determine whether a marriage has been contracted and the civil consequences that follow. It cannot supply an exception to a criminal law where Parliament has provided none."The court clarified that it was not deciding whether the nikah was valid, void or voidable. Even if the marriage were assumed to be valid, it said, that would not take sexual intercourse with a person below 18 outside the scope of POCSO or the BNS. The court also rejected the argument that the girl's consent or the absence of force and coercion could take the case outside POCSO.“POCSO does not confer such a power upon the child, her parents, or the Court,” it observed.The court further said that the age difference between the couple did not by itself establish guilt, but was relevant while considering whether the court should exercise its exceptional jurisdiction to terminate a POCSO prosecution at the threshold.The HC also rejected the argument that the FIR was unsustainable because neither the girl nor her family had approached the police, adding in this case, once doctors learnt that the pregnant patient was below 18, the statutory reporting mechanism was triggered, the court said.The court also rejected the petitioners' reliance on constitutional freedoms under Articles 21, 25 and 26, holding that they could not create an exception to a generally applicable penal law enacted for the protection of children.“Constitutional liberty protects choice; it does not create an exception to POCSO or the BNS,” the judgment said.The court cautioned against an interpretation that would effectively introduce a marital exception into POCSO for children below 18.Justice Narula added that, “The statutory protection would then depend not upon the age of the child, but upon whether a marriage had been arranged before the sexual relationship was discovered. That would turn the legislation on its head."“The conclusion is narrower: a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, by reason of that status alone, confer immunity from POCSO or BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time. Any other view would create, through judicial decision, an exception which Parliament has expressly excluded,” he added.The court acknowledged that individual cases may involve “affection rather than violence, and relationships rather than predation”, but said such circumstances could not permit courts to rewrite the statutory definition of an offence.Dismissing the petition, the High Court held that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, merely because of that status, confer immunity from POCSO or the BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: A 56-year-old man was killed after a fallen tree struck him in Brooklyn on Saturday as a powerful early-season storm, known as a nor’easter, battered the US Northeast with heavy rain and strong winds.Emergency crews were called to Euclid Avenue between Dumont Avenue and Linden Boulevard shortly before 3:30 pm, according to the New York City Fire Department (FDNY).First responders found the man suffering from severe trauma and took him to a hospital, where he later died. Authorities have not released his identity.The storm has brought strong winds, heavy rain, coastal flooding and high surf across the Northeast, affecting areas from North Carolina to New England.In New York City, winds reached up to 55 mph, while gusts of up to 60 mph remained possible through Sunday, according to city emergency officials.The nor’easter also disrupted air travel, with hundreds of flights cancelled and thousands delayed across the region.Nearly 73,000 homes and businesses were without power at one point on Saturday, although the number had fallen from an earlier peak of about 119,000.Officials have warned residents about dangerous flooding and high tides, urging them to stay away from beaches and flooded areas. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said anyone going near the water during the storm was “literally gambling with their life”.The storm also forced the cancellation of concerts and sporting events, including scheduled shows by singer Ed Sheeran in Massachusetts.The National Weather Service said the storm could continue to bring strong winds, heavy rain and high tides into early next week. Coastal flooding is expected to remain a concern during high tides, with some areas forecast to see water levels several feet above normal.The governors of New York and New Jersey had declared states of emergency in areas expected to be hit hardest by the storm.You use AI every day. articles.title: British woman shot dead by father after argument over Donald Trump; grand jury ruled death accidental, mother seeks fresh probe
articles.summary: Jane Coates, mother of Lucy Harrison, is urging a new investigation into her daughter's tragic death after a Texas grand jury ruled the shooting accidental. Independent experts challenge the father's account and raise serious questions about the police investigation.
articles.body: The mother of a 23-year-old British woman shot dead by her father in Texas is seeking a fresh investigation into her daughter’s death after a US grand jury ruled the shooting accidental.Jane Coates is travelling from England to Texas to ask the Collin County District Attorney’s Office to reconsider the case involving her daughter, Lucy Harrison, who was killed on January 10 last year.Lucy had travelled from the UK with her boyfriend, Sam Littler, to visit her father, Kris Harrison, and her two younger half-sisters.Hours before the shooting, Lucy and her father had a heated argument about President Donald Trump, who was due to be inaugurated for a second term, The New York Post reported.Harrison, 52, told police that his Glock 9mm pistol discharged accidentally when he took it from a box after Lucy asked whether he had a gun.“It just went off as she stood there, like as I pulled it out it went off,” Harrison said in a police video provided to a UK inquest into Lucy’s death.A grand jury later declined to bring manslaughter or criminally negligent homicide charges against Harrison after determining that Lucy’s death was accidental.Coates is now questioning that conclusion and wants investigators to examine evidence presented by independent experts.“I simply want the truth about what happened,” Coates told The Post. “I want the people responsible for investigating her death to sit down with us and listen to what we have been told by independent experts.”Questions over how Lucy was killedCraig Miller, a retired Dallas deputy chief and former homicide detective with more than 30 years of experience, has disputed Harrison’s account after reviewing bodycam footage, police reports and Lucy’s autopsy findings.“Guns just don’t go off,” Miller told the outlet. “The only person who could have fired the gun is the dad. He may not have been familiar with the gun but there was a bullet in the chamber.”Miller also questioned the direction of the bullet and the circumstances described by Harrison.“If that was true, why didn’t the bullet come in through the side? It entered directly through the center of the chest,” he said.“It was fired at a downward trajectory and that is not consistent … this does not add up.”Miller also raised questions about the police investigation, including whether Harrison underwent a gunshot residue test and whether investigators examined the phones belonging to Harrison and Lucy.“I don’t think the officers checked that, which I think is key,” Miller said. “[That] would have made it simpler and better for everybody else to look at the case properly.”The grand jury’s notes remain sealed, making it unclear what evidence was presented to the panel.Miller said investigators should have considered Harrison’s account alongside evidence about his condition at the time of the shooting.“If the facts didn’t include that he was intoxicated and the forensics did not match up with how he said the gun went off, then the grand jury should be made aware,” he said.UK inquest reached different conclusionA separate inquest in the UK also raised questions about the circumstances surrounding Lucy’s death.Jacqueline Devonish, senior coroner for Cheshire, described Harrison as a “functioning alcoholic” and disputed his account of the shooting.“To shoot her through the chest whilst she was standing would have required him to have been pointing the gun at his daughter, without checking for bullets, and pulling the trigger,” Devonish told the inquest.She concluded that Lucy had been “unlawfully killed” and said her father’s actions amounted to gross negligence manslaughter.The UK coroner’s finding does not have binding effect in US courts.Miller also pointed to bodycam footage showing Harrison initially denying to an officer that he had been drinking. It later emerged that he had consumed a 17-ounce carton of white wine that day, according to the report.“The dad lied to the police in the very first question asked,” Miller said. “When a person lies and is inconsistent with their testimony, those are important facts for the police to look at and consider.”Harrison previously said through his lawyer that he “fully accepted” the consequences of his actions and that “there isn’t a day I don’t feel the weight of that loss, a weight I will carry for the rest of my life.”Coates said her focus was on ensuring her daughter was remembered beyond the circumstances of her death.“There isn’t a day that goes by when I don’t think about Lucy and everything she should have had in front of her,” she told The Post. “I want people to see her as a person, not just as a case. She was funny, kind, loving and full of life. She had dreams. She had people who loved her deeply. She deserved a future.”Prosper Police have confirmed that the department will not reopen the investigation.A spokesperson for the Town of Prosper said: “We have great empathy for Lucy’s family and recognize that the loss of a child is an unimaginable tragedy.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Christa Barfield, the former Philadelphia healthcare worker who switched careers after a 2018 trip to Martinique; she now runs a 123-acre farm in West Chester and is opening a food-and-medicine store
articles.summary: Christa Barfield grew up in Germantown, Philadelphia, and once worked in healthcare.
articles.body: Christa Barfield grew up in Germantown, Philadelphia, and once worked in healthcare. Her career changed after a 2018 trip to Martinique, where she met Black farmers and saw their work first-hand. Five days after returning home, Barfield began planning a new career in farming.Today, the 38-year-old St. Joseph’s University graduate runs FarmerJawn Agriculture in West Chester, outside Philadelphia. According to Philadelphia Tribune, The farm covers 128 acres and employs 26 people. Barfield says it is the largest Black-owned farm in Pennsylvania that grows food.Her work now goes beyond growing crops. FarmerJawn has locations in West Chester, Kensington and Elkins Park, with each location following a different farming model. West Chester is rural, Elkins Park is suburban and Kensington is urban. Barfield wants to show that farming and access to food can work across all three settings.The next step is the planned opening of CornerJawn, a food and medicine corner store in Kensington. Scheduled to open on October 1, the store is part of Barfield’s effort to bring FarmerJawn’s produce closer to Philadelphia communities.A career change after MartiniqueBarfield’s decision to enter farming began with her trip to Martinique in 2018. While on the island, she met Black farmers, and the experience changed how she thought about her own career.“I got on a plane to Martinique, and I met Black farmers while I was on the island, and what I saw inspired me,” Barfield told the Philadelphia Tribune. “I came home five days later and started planning to become a farmer.”After returning to Philadelphia, she started working towards becoming a farmer. Her early business was funded through gig work. She delivered groceries for Uber, Lyft and Instacart while building FarmerJawn.The journey also came with challenges. Barfield has spoken about the difficulties of being a Black farm owner. At the same time, she said communities in Philadelphia and West Chester have supported her work.Her farming operation has since grown into a larger network. The West Chester farm is based on the campus of Westtown School. The campus has had a farm in operation since 1799.From a 128-acre farm to city neighbourhoodsDuring a recent tour of the farm, the Philadelphia Tribune saw rows of tomatoes, corn, watermelons and collard greens, along with other produce.Barfield describes the farm as regenerative and organic. She also aims to make FarmerJawn one of the only such Black-owned farms in the world.Her focus is not limited to what happens on the farm. She wants the produce to reach Philadelphia neighbourhoods, including communities that may not have easy access to the food grown at the farm.“We're really working on building a relationship, cleaning up the food system, and making the food system better,” she said. “Growing food and building storefronts in urban areas to make sure this food gets to communities that need it.”That approach is also behind CornerJawn in Kensington. Barfield wants the store to connect residents with regenerative and organic food while also helping them understand where their food comes from.“All of those residents in Kensington deserve regenerative and organic food, and they all deserve to know where their food comes from and who their farmer is,” she said. “Our commercial corridors should not leave anyone out, and that's what CornerJawn is we're going to build something really dope.”Teaching farming to the next generationBarfield also wants FarmerJawn’s work to have an educational role. She hopes to partner with schools so students can learn about farming.For Barfield, the connection between farming and the Black community is also important because of its historical significance. She wants the Black community to embrace farming and see it as part of its history.The three FarmerJawn locations are part of that wider approach. The company’s West Chester operation represents rural farming, while the Elkins Park location represents a suburban setting. Kensington provides an urban model.Barfield wants to demonstrate that these different settings can all support farming and access to food. The planned CornerJawn store will add another part to that model by bringing food and medicine into a Philadelphia neighbourhood.Building something that can be replicatedBarfield says she sees her work as more than a personal career change. She also understands the visibility that comes with running a Black-owned farming business.“I don't take it lightly (responsibility of being an inspiration to Black and brown people). I am just a girl from Germantown who is a mother, a daughter, who wants to just be good to people,” she said.Her goal is to build something that can be repeated elsewhere. “Building something beautiful that can be replicated in other parts of the world,” Barfield said.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Julius Hunter allegedly lured a teen to a fake $300 babysitting job on Craigslist before a hours-long sexual assault at a Clarkston apartment.
articles.body: Georgia investigators are searching for potential victims of a convicted Florida sex offender after DNA linked him to three sexual assault cases involving women allegedly lured through Craigslist job ads. Julius Hunter, 42, faces rape, aggravated sodomy and kidnapping charges in Georgia in connection with a 2016 attack on a 19-year-old teen at a Clarkston apartment complex. A DeKalb County grand jury indicted him on Aug. 11. Before his Georgia arrest, Hunter pleaded no contest in an unrelated 2021 Florida sexual battery case involving his former girlfriend. Investigators are now examining what they believe is a broader pattern of sexual assaults. FIANCÉE STICKS BY ACCUSED SERIAL RAPIST AS SPECIAL AGENTS DEFEND TAILING HIM FOR RESTAURANT DNA STAKEOUT "Hunter grew up in New Jersey, so it is possible there may be victims there," DeKalb County District Attorney Investigator Brandi Rogers told Fox News Digital. Hunter's DNA also matched evidence from two additional sexual assault cases in DeKalb and Gwinnett counties in 2016 and 2017, authorities said. REPEAT OFFENDER WITH 7 PRIOR CONVICTIONS ARRESTED 3 TIMES IN 12 DAYS OVER ALLEGED ATTACKS ON WOMEN He has not been charged in either case. Rogers said investigators have been unable to reconnect with the two women. $300 babysitting job The 19-year-old thought she was heading to a $300 overnight babysitting job when Hunter arranged a ride-share to an apartment near 700 Jolly Avenue on July 27, 2016, according to the DeKalb County District Attorney’s Office. When she arrived, there were no children — only Hunter and another man, authorities said. She attempted to leave, but Hunter allegedly stopped her and sexually assaulted her over several hours before releasing her the following day. DNA TECHNOLOGY LEADS TO ARREST IN 1988 KILLING OF ORLANDO WOMAN AFTER NEARLY FOUR DECADES The woman fled in a cab and asked the driver to call 911. She then met police officers at a gas station before going to a hospital for a sexual assault exam. Rogers told Fox News Digital that investigators have not identified the second man inside the apartment and continue to seek information about him. He has not been charged. Florida arrest leads to DNA match The Clarkston case remained unsolved for years after the Georgia Bureau of Investigation developed a male DNA profile from the 19-year-old’s sexual assault kit. The profile was entered into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) but, at the time, did not match anyone in the national database. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X That changed after Hunter's 2021 Florida conviction. Authorities collected his DNA and entered his profile into CODIS, triggering a match to DNA recovered from the Clarkston sexual assault kits, along with the sexual assault kits collected in the DeKalb and Gwinnett counties cases. Authorities arrested Hunter in Fort Lauderdale on Aug. 13, two days after the DeKalb County grand jury indicted him. He was extradited to Georgia and booked into the DeKalb County Jail on Aug. 20. Don Plummer, a spokesperson for the Georgia Public Defender Council, which is representing Hunter, declined to comment on the case. Authorities said Hunter used Craigslist ads to solicit women for jobs involving "babysitting, modeling, dancing and massages." articles.title: In 2018, Jon Bon Jovi paid $10 million for a Palm Beach home, demolished it and rebuilt; two years later he sold the new mansion for $19.85 million and bought a $43 million estate
articles.summary: American rock icon Jon Bon Jovi turned a $10 million land purchase into a major Palm Beach real estate upgrade, selling his custom-built home for nearly
articles.body: American rock icon Jon Bon Jovi turned a $10 million land purchase into a major Palm Beach real estate upgrade, selling his custom-built home for nearly twice what he paid for the land before buying a much larger oceanfront estate nearby. Property records and reports from The Real Deal show the singer sold his custom-built Palm Beach home for $19.85 million. On the same day, he bought a larger beachfront mansion for $43 million. The two deals became one of Bon Jovi's most notable real estate moves in the exclusive South Florida town.Redeveloping on North Ocean BoulevardBon Jovi first entered the Palm Beach market in 2018. He paid $10 million for an oceanfront property at 230 N. Ocean Blvd. through a limited liability company. The property had an older house on it, which he and his wife, Dorothea Hurley, tore down to make room for a new home. In its place, they built a custom Italian-style home of a little more than 5,000 square feet. The finished house had five bedrooms, five full bathrooms and three half-bathrooms. It also had oak and limestone floors, cypress ceilings, a library, an elevator and a two-car garage. The property included a courtyard, a swimming pool, landscaped outdoor areas and a loggia. It also had direct beach access. The home was listed for $22.9 million in May 2020. It sold about two months later for $19.85 million, according to Realtor.com. The recorded sale price was $19,847,000. The sale price was well above Bon Jovi's original $10 million land purchase, although the cost of demolishing the old house and building the new one would have reduced the overall profit. The buyer was a trust affiliated with Rob Posner, CEO of NewDay USA, according to Palm Beach Daily News reporting carried by Yahoo News.Upgrading to a Larger Oceanfront EstateBon Jovi did not wait long to make his next move. On the same day his custom-built home sold, he closed on a $43 million oceanfront mansion at 1075 N. Ocean Blvd., according to property records and The Real Deal's reporting. The new estate was much larger than the home he had just sold. Built in 2007, the Mediterranean-style mansion covers about 10,232 square feet. It was designed by architect Thomas Kirchhoff, with interiors by David Kleinberg. The house has seven bedrooms, seven full bathrooms and five powder rooms. It also includes a formal dining room, a temperature-controlled wine cellar, a home gym, an elevator and staff or guest quarters. Outside, the property has a private courtyard, a swimming pool, two oceanfront loggias and direct beach access. Other features include an ocean-facing library, a large owner's suite, a chef's kitchen and a three-car garage. The property had originally been listed for $44.9 million before Bon Jovi bought it for $43 million.Resisting the Palm Beach Land RushBon Jovi's move came as Palm Beach was seeing a wave of high-end real estate deals. Wealthy buyers were seeking large properties, privacy and Florida's tax advantages. Some buyers were also purchasing older homes and land with plans to create much larger estates. Years later, Bon Jovi's $43 million property became part of another major Palm Beach real estate story. According to The Wall Street Journal and Realtor.com, an unidentified buyer began assembling several properties near Mar-a-Lago, spending roughly $250 million. The purchases included two oceanfront parcels formerly owned by cosmetics heir William Lauder. The parcels covered about 2.8 acres and sold for close to $200 million, with reports putting the price near $178 million. Bon Jovi's estate sits next to the assembled properties. Reports said the buyer had approached him about selling, but his property remained outside the growing assemblage. The result is an unusual position for the rock star. What began with a $10 million Palm Beach land purchase became a $19.85 million home sale and, on the same day, a $43 million upgrade to a much larger oceanfront estate.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 'American terrorist army': Iran claims second US submarine seized in Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy has claimed it captured a second advanced US unmanned underwater vehicle, the Remus 600, in the
articles.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy has claimed it captured a second advanced US unmanned underwater vehicle, the Remus 600, in the Strait of Hormuz.According to a statement carried by Iranian state broadcaster IRIB on Sunday, the operation targeted what Iranian military authorities described as the "second subsurface [submarine] of the American terrorist army" operating in the strategic waterway.The IRGC said the operation was carried out through a "coordinated and complex operation" involving military intelligence and electronic warfare capabilities."With the help of God Almighty, the IRGC navy soldiers, through a coordinated and complex operation with intelligence and electronic warfare, were able to trap an advanced UAV of the American terrorist army that was operating in the Strait of Hormuz for the purpose of espionage," the statement read.The IRGC Navy identified the captured platform as a Remus 600, an autonomous unmanned underwater vehicle. Iranian officials alleged that it was carrying out espionage missions inside the strait."This submersible is a type of intelligent and advanced submersible called the Remus 600, which was captured by the IRGC navy and is now in the hands of the force's specialists to retrieve its information," it added.IRIB said the captured vehicle had been handed over to specialist military technicians, who would analyse the system and recover its stored data.The IRGC navy also reiterated its position on maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, declaring the waterway closed and warning that it would continue taking "strong and relentless" action against unauthorised traffic."The IRGC navy firmly declares that the Strait of Hormuz is closed and we are taking strong and relentless action against dangerous movements and unauthorised traffic through the Strait of Hormuz," the statement added.Iran vows no retreatThe claim came as Iranian leaders continued to signal that Tehran would not back down in its confrontation with the US and Israel.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said earlier on Sunday that Tehran would remain resolute, after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.Speaking to people gathered at an airport after his return from the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Pezeshkian said, “We stand firm with strength, we are at the service of our people, we will stand until our last breath, and we promise that as long as we have life in our bodies, we will be honest servants to the people; you have put us to shame, I do not consider myself worthy of your presence, I am your servant.”Iranian Armed Forces senior spokesperson Brigadier General Abolfazl Shekarchi also said Tehran had resolved “to have not the slightest retreat in the face of the enemy and to suppress him.”Shekarchi said Iran was “the most experienced country in the world in asymmetric warfare” and warned the US against interfering in the management of the Strait of Hormuz.“The Americans should not dream of interfering in the management of the Strait of Hormuz, and if they interfere, they will receive a slap from the Iranian Armed Forces; they must leave our region,” he said.He further warned, “Any ship that passes through the Strait of Hormuz outside the route designated by Iran will not have security.”Iran's ceasefire proposalPezeshkian and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi had earlier travelled to the US for the UN gathering of world leaders, where Tehran proposed a seven-day roadmap aimed at ending the fighting and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.Under the proposal, Washington would lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales, release an estimated $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets and observe a ceasefire covering the region, including Lebanon and Yemen.In return, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while negotiations with the US on a final agreement over Tehran's nuclear programme would begin on the seventh day. Araghchi said the initial steps would take four to five days, with the waterway reopening on the sixth day.Trump, however, rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire.You use AI every day. articles.title: Are there no Virat Kohli fans in Kerala? Rohit Sharma 'Hitman' mania steals the show during India vs West Indies ODI
articles.summary: While fans remain excited to see the return of both Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, Hitman's fans in Thiruvananthapuram have vastly outnumbered Kohli fans in K...
articles.body:
This could be the last time Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli play an international match for India in Kerala.

Rohit's welcome, including a 50-foot cutout, dominated social media in Thiruvananthapuram.

Kohli's fan base showed up too, with a 12x30-foot banner unveiled at Greenfield Stadium.

Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma are already making waves in Kerala

Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have shared a dressing room for close to two decades, but their visit to Kerala for the 1st ODI against the West Indies is an emotional one. Both men play only a single format for India, and this could be the last time both legends feature in a game in the state.

However, neither has ruled out the match as their final international appearance in the state.

That backdrop turned Thiruvananthapuram into something closer to a farewell tour than a routine series opener. Fan clubs for both players spent the days before the match building tributes, banners, and cutouts around the Greenfield Stadium, determined to make the occasion memorable. What followed was not a quiet split of affection either.

While on the global stage, supporters often split evenly between the Hitman and the King, that wasn't the case in Kerala's capital city. Rohit's supporters went several steps further than Kohli's, and social media noticed almost immediately.

Why this could be Rohit and Kohli's last game in Kerala

Neither man has confirmed retirement outright. But the signs suggest that this is the case. Kohli has already said 2027 will be his last World Cup for India. Rohit has been vague, but he, too, now plays only the 50-over format.

Kerala's cricket calendar does not offer many chances to host India. If the match genuinely is a farewell, both fan bases were determined to mark the occasion properly. Rohit's supporters simply made more noise about it.

Star Sports India set the mood before a ball was bowled. "When the Hitman returns, the welcome has to be larger than life! Rohit Sharma is set to return for the 1st ODI vs West Indies, and Thiruvananthapuram is already buzzing," the post read.

How Kerala celebrated Rohit Sharma's return

Rohit's fan base did not hold back. One account described the mood on the ground. "Cake cutting and Mumbai Cha Raja Rohit Sharma chants. Kerala going crazy for Hitman," the post read. While the cricketing world has seen the same scenes in Mumbai numerous times, to see the same fanfare in Kerala has been genuinely heartwarming.

Rohit's official fan association shared scenes from the ground with a simple caption: "Scenes from Trivandrum." The tweet showed droves of fans cutting cakes with Hitman's images on them as the fans celebrated his return to the stadium.

The same account followed up with a warmer message, simply captioned "Our Family." This time the post showed multiple members of the fan club with an enormous banner of Rohit Sharma.

The centerpiece, however, was impossible to miss. Journalist Rahul Rawat described its scale.

In the midst of all this madness, Kohli's fans were much harder to spot despite Kohli's excellent record in the state.

Virat Kohli's fans made their presence felt too

Kerala does have plenty of Kohli fans. His supporters, the AKVKFA, unveiled a striking tribute of their own inside the stadium grounds. The caption on their Instagram post read :

"A Journey of Passion, Pride, and Unforgettable Career. AKVKFA is celebrating the legacy, honouring the moments with a great tribute to our idol king Kohli. A 12x30-foot banner at Trivandrum Greenfield Stadium."

One fan summed up what Kerala's cricket-loving crowd wanted most from the day. "Kerala fans, you're the best. India wins the match, and Virat Kohli also scores runs in that victory; there could be no better gift for you than that," the post read.

Kohli's welcome was genuine and heartfelt. It simply arrived at a lower volume. Rohit FC had decided, well in advance, that Kerala's biggest tribute belonged to their man, and on the ground itself, it was difficult to argue they didn't get their wish.

However, as both men move towards the twilight of their careers, it's hard to say they aren't two of the most popular figures that the sport has given India.

articles.title: Paige Spiranac welcomes fall golf by revisiting summer fun, Allie Rae geared up for Vikings in Tampa & meat
articles.summary: Paige Spiranac bid farewell to summer golf with a highlight reel, while Big Ten football saw shocking upsets for Michigan, USC, and Penn State.
articles.body: It's Sunday, and I am back after taking a couple of days off last week. More on that in a minute. But first up on the Screencaps agenda today is the transition from summer to fall. It's about putting the swimsuits and short shorts away and reaching for the sweatshirts and warmer clothing. It's also about properly paying your respects to the summer that was. When you're in the content game and considered one of the best, like golf's top influencer Paige Spiranac, bidding adieu to summer while looking forward to fall shouldn't be difficult. SYDNEY THOMAS MOCKS LANE KIFFIN AFTER LOSS WITH BRUTAL HALLOWEEN COSTUME IDEA, LSU FANS FIGHT & NATE'S SHORTS That is, of course, if you're not overthinking it. Any up-and-coming influencers out there, take a page from Paige's playbook and revisit summer with a highlight package of some of your best work. This isn't about trying to outproduce anyone with the content. It's about respect. When you give it, you receive it. Here's how one of the best to ever do it approached it. "Saying goodbye to summer golf and hello to fall golf😍," Paige wrote. "but first wanted to revisit some summer golf fun⛳️" There's another lesson to be learned from this and that's to keep your foot on the gas. You won't see Paige Spiranac blowing many leads at home. She keeps at it no matter how far out in front she is. PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE The same can't be said for Michigan It was a tough day for some Big Ten teams at home on Saturday. Most notably for No. 12 USC, who ended up losing 41-27 to No. 20 Oregon. And for No. 18 Michigan, who didn't have any extra time available during their 20-19 walk-off loss to No. 17 Iowa. The Michigan loss, which you really hate to see, produced real art. Take a look at this touchdown and the reaction from the Wolverine student section. The shock. The horror. The stunned silence of a loss in a game they were seconds away from winning. Again, you really hate to see it. Of course, there was another ranked Big Ten team who lost at home and blew a lead while doing so. I'm well aware of No. 13 ranked Penn State losing to unranked Wisconsin at home and blowing a 17-point lead. But I was under the impression that James Franklin was no longer the head coach and that ugly losses were a thing of the past. Although to be fair to Franklin, up until his last season, he didn’t lose these types of games all that often. It's the wakeup call Penn State needed. They haven’t played anyone yet, despite my attempt to pretend that they have by ignoring their soft schedule (which I will do again). The Meats - Homebrew Bill writes: Beef tri tip, pork tenderloin, and chicken. At least I'll have leftovers this week. SeanJo Better late than never. This is one of the emails I received over the last couple of weeks that I'm just getting to. Homebrew Bill, as always, your meat looks fantastic. Keep the emails coming. Sunday afternoon grill reward - Socal desert Mike writes: My cardiologist doesn't care for me to do this, but a Man's gotta have meat some days. Thanks for all you do! SeanJo I'd argue with you if I could. Thanks for the support and thanks for sharing your meat. Send it in whenever you have meat on the menu. I want to see it. articles.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
articles.summary: The two attacks hours apart come as the country struggles to stop high levels of gang-related armed violence.
articles.body:
Twenty-seven people have been killed in two mass shootings hours apart in South Africa, the latest gun violence to hit the country.

Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar close to Johannesburg on Saturday evening, with 15 more injured.

In a separate shooting in the early hours of Sunday morning, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town and a further 11 were injured.

South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world and has struggled to contain gang-related gun violence in recent years. Police have not given a definitive motive for either of the latest attacks.

In Johannesburg, gunmen opened fire on customers outside the bar before continuing the attack inside and torching two vehicles before fleeing.

Police said thirteen men and four women were killed.

Gauteng Police Commissioner Lt Gen Tommy Mthombeni said people from Ethiopia and Lesotho were among those caught up in the shooting, but that the vast majority were South African.

He also said police believed the motive behind the shooting was robbery, as personal belongings had been taken, but that they could not rule out turf wars between illegal mining groups.

Earlier, deputy provincial police commissioner Maj Gen Fred Kekana said the attack may have been a retaliation for an incident last month, in which one person was killed and another wounded, according to news agency AFP.

He said at the scene that police had clear pictures and in some cases names for the suspects.

In Cape Town, five victims died at the scene and a further five people died in hospital.

No arrests had been made in either case on Sunday morning.

The two mass shootings came days after 11 people were killed in the city of Durban when gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township.

Illegal weapons are prevalent in South Africa and gun violence has been a persistent problem for decades, with about 60 murders recorded every day in the country of 62 million.

But a recent spate of mass shootings has raised fears that the problem is deepening, with violence often linked to turf wars between gangs engaged in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa called organised crime "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year, the military was deployed alongside police in areas with the highest murder rates in an effort to reduce armed violence.

On Saturday, a tenth woman's body was found in Ekurhuleni , to the east of Johannesburg, with local police saying they were unable to rule out a serial killer operating in the area with similarities between the deaths.
